title: Keyturn Host Protection Plan: a Host's Withdrawal of Their Own Claim
content:
A host may take their own claim back off the enrolment, and doing so releases money that stands booked as owed to them on the enrolment's claims. What is not released stays owed on the enrolment. The withdrawal stands against the claim it closes on the Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment the claim was made under.

### Situation of use and capability

`withdraw_own_claim_4cdcc89b` writes a withdrawal record against the named claim and releases the money that was standing booked as owed to the host on it, reducing the enrolment's balance owed to the host by that figure. The host can afterwards see the claim closed by their withdrawal and the lower amount owed to them.

### How it is invoked

The tool is unlocked and then handed over to be run by the customer themselves: the claim is the host's own and the withdrawal is the host's own act, performed in person rather than by the desk on their behalf.

### Parameters

- `enrollment_id` — the reference number of the host protection enrolment the claim was made under, read from the enrolment record retrieved for this host.
- `source_claim_id` — the reference number of the claim record being withdrawn, read from the claim records standing on that enrolment.
- `booking_id` — the reference number of the trip booking the withdrawn claim was made against, read from that claim record.
- `damage_category` — the kind of loss the withdrawn claim covered, one of `exterior_body`, `interior`, `glass`, `tyres_wheels`, `mechanical`, `theft_total_loss`, `missing_equipment` and `third_party_property`.
- `released_amount` — the money released back from what was booked as owed to the host on the withdrawn claim, in USD, 2 decimal places, signed, passed as a positive figure rounded half-up to the cent.

### Return

A confirmation line in plain text carrying the reference number of the withdrawal record, the claim it closes, the amount released in USD to the cent and the enrolment's new balance owed to the host. Receiving that line means the claim is withdrawn; no other output is produced.
